content: Insulin resistance decreases significantly immediately after childbirth, necessitating modifications in diabetes management strategies. A contraceptive plan should be discussed and established for all individuals with diabetes who are of childbearing potential. Individuals with a recent history of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) should undergo screening for diabetes at 4 to 12 weeks postpartum using the 75-gram oral glucose tolerance test and diagnostic criteria appropriate for nonpregnant individuals. Individuals with overweight or obesity and a history of GDM who are found to have prediabetes should be provided with intensive lifestyle interventions and/or metformin therapy to prevent the progression to diabetes. Breastfeeding is recommended for all individuals with diabetes as part of postpartum care. Individuals with a history of GDM should undergo lifelong screening for the development of type 2 diabetes or prediabetes at intervals of every 1 to 3 years. Individuals with a history of GDM should pursue preconception screening for diabetes and preconception care to identify and manage hyperglycemia, thereby reducing the risk of congenital malformations. Postpartum care should include a psychosocial assessment and support to promote effective self-care practices.
